newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares end slightly up, profit taking seen.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares end slightly up, profit taking seen.

text.p: Israeli shares closed a shade higher on balance on Monday despite some profit taking, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.33 percent, or 0.85 points to 260.25 on an all-share turnover of 144 million shekels, against 116 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.13 percent higher at 269.26.
"The Maof faces strong resistance at 270 and I believe that the market will stabilse at the current level if nothing dramatic happens," said a trader at Tachlit Securities.
"Activity was relatively high today and the market continues to rise. The market is still very strong but investors were taking profits today," said a trader at Bank Leumi.

The most active shares were Leumi Insurance, which rose 3.75 percent to 216 agorot on volume of 10.5 million shekels, and Israel Discount Bank which fell 1.75 percent to 360 agorot on turnover of 9.6 million shekels.
General Bank surged six percent to 11,107 agorot on volume of 7.3 million shekels. Traders said the share rose following the company's rights issue on Sunday.
